summary: For St James’s Hospital, the first step is a complaint to the hospital’s Patient Experience Office / HSE route, with a 12‑month complaint window shown in the hospital leaflet and staged response times on the HSE site. If that does not sort it out, the independent route is the Ombudsman, usually after the hospital’s final response or review. Compensation for delayed diagnosis here is a clinical-negligence court claim, not an Injuries Resolution Board claim, and public-hospital claims are handled on the defence side through the State Claims Agency.

steps.what: For a complaint about care in a public hospital, the independent reviewer is the Office of the Ombudsman. You normally go there after complaining to the provider and using its appeal or review process, though the Ombudsman says you can complain sooner if there is a long delay in the provider replying.
steps.deadline: "We cannot look into a complaint if it is made more than 12 months after you initially complained of the action or you became aware of that action, unless there are very special circumstances"

steps.body: State Claims Agency / Courts Service / Injuries Resolution Board
steps.what: For alleged harm from public-hospital care in Ireland, the compensation route is a clinical-negligence claim in court, not an Injuries Resolution Board assessment. In claims against covered public-health bodies, the State Claims Agency says the State authority remains the legal defendant while the Agency takes over responsibility for resolving the claim, and it may use mediation or go to trial.
steps.deadline: "shall not be brought after the expiration of three years from the date on which the cause of action accrued or the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured."
points: Medical negligence claims are excluded from the Injuries Resolution Board.
The State Claims Agency says covered public-health claims are handled under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme.
The Scheme covers the HSE and voluntary health and social care organisations indemnified by the Minister for Health, and the State Claims Agency list includes "St. James’s Hospital Board".
The statutory limitation period is three years from the cause of action or the later date of knowledge.
The High Court has a dedicated Clinical Negligence List for these proceedings.
requires: A clinical-negligence/personal-injuries claim rather than a general service complaint
The defendant body must be covered by the Clinical Indemnity Scheme for State Claims Agency handling
steps.appliesIf: Alleged injury from public-hospital clinical care in Ireland, including claims involving St. James’s Hospital Board under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme.
alternatives: Complaint to St James’s / HSE about the care
Independent complaint to the Ombudsman after the provider route
Alternative dispute resolution such as mediation during claim resolution
missing: Exact date of knowledge if different from the dates in the timeline
Whether the patient wants only an explanation/apology or also damages
Whether surgery or later losses may change the value and court level

sources.quote: medical negligence claims are not included in the accidents we can assess.

The Personal Injuries Assessment Board Act 2003, as amended, excludes claims “arising out of the provision of any health service to a person, the carrying out of a medical or surgical procedure in relation to a person or the provision of any medical advice or treatment to a person”.

When a claim is made against a State authority under the Clinical Indemnity Scheme, the State authority remains the legal defendant and the State Claims Agency takes over responsibility for resolving the claim.
Offering and engaging in alternative dispute resolution methods, such as mediation, and in settlement negotiations
shall not be brought after the expiration of three years from the date on which the cause of action accrued or the date of knowledge (if later) of the person injured.

The Clinical Negligence List shall encompass all proceedings in which a claim for damages for personal injuries arises from alleged negligence or breach of duty in the provision of clinical or health care, treatment, or advice (“clinical negligence proceedings”).

steps.body: Legal Aid Board / Irish Statute Book / Legal Services Regulatory Authority
steps.what: The Legal Aid Board says it can provide legal advice and representation in medical negligence, subject to financial eligibility and, for court representation, a merits test. The official sources in this run also show that charging a percentage of damages is prohibited, but they do not clearly confirm whether any broader conditional-fee arrangement is lawful for this type of claim.
points: The Legal Aid Board says it can provide legal advice and legal representation in medical negligence.
To qualify financially, disposable income must be under €18,000.
The Board’s online calculator only checks whether you might financially qualify; it does not decide whether your case will actually get legal aid.
If you need representation in court, the Board says it will examine the merits of your case.
The LSRA says advertisements for personal-injury legal services must not use phrases such as “no win no fee” that could suggest the services are at no cost.
steps.appliesIf: An adult in Ireland seeking legal aid for a medical-negligence claim.
alternatives: Private solicitor funding arrangements, which would need to be checked directly with the solicitor
missing: Household income and asset details for the Legal Aid Board means test
Whether the patient wants advice only or full representation
Whether any solicitor has offered a private funding arrangement

steps.body: National Clinical Effectiveness Committee / HSE National Central Repository
steps.what: In Ireland’s public system, national clinical guidelines are overseen by the National Clinical Effectiveness Committee, and HSE national clinical guidelines are stored in the HSE National Central Repository. The HSE’s development guide also shows a specific HSE National Clinical Guidelines working group.
points: The NCEC oversees the National Clinical Guidelines.
The HSE National Central Repository is the single trusted source for HSE national policies, procedures, protocols, guidelines and clinical guidelines.
The HSE development guide refers to an HSE National Clinical Guidelines working group chaired by the Head of the Evidence and Quality Hub.
steps.appliesIf: Looking for the national clinical guidance bodies and repositories used in Irish public healthcare.

steps.what: The free independent help route is the Patient Advocacy Service. It says it supports patients of Public Acute Hospitals to make complaints, and it can also support people after a patient safety incident.
points: The service says it is independent, free and confidential.
It supports complaints about care in Public Acute Hospitals.
It can also support people in the aftermath of a Patient Safety Incident.
The HSE complaints pages also signpost Patient Advocacy Service and other advocacy bodies for help with complaints.
steps.appliesIf: A patient in a public acute hospital in Ireland wants free independent help with a complaint or a patient safety incident.
alternatives: Other advocacy bodies listed by the HSE, including Citizens Information and Irish Patients’ Association

steps.what: St James’s Hospital routes patient medical-records requests through its Access to Information Office. Its page offers a Subject Access Request form and says it handles routine and administrative access requests for healthcare records; national GDPR guidance says the organisation should respond within one month, subject to a possible extension.
points: St James’s says its Access to Information Office handles routine and administrative requests from patients for healthcare records.
The page gives the Access to Information Office contact email aio@stjames.ie.
The hospital page links a Subject Access Request (SAR) form and an FOI Patient Record Request Form.
The Data Protection Commission says the controller must respond without undue delay and in any event within one month.
The one-month period may be extended by two further months if necessary, but the controller must tell you within one month and explain why.
steps.appliesIf: A patient wants a copy of their records from St James’s Hospital.
alternatives: Use the St James’s FOI Patient Record Request Form if that route is more suitable
missing: Whether the patient wants all records or just the emergency-department and imaging records
